title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Suggested That Neutrophils Predominated the Airways of Children With the Respiratory Syncytial Virus.
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a predominant aetiology of early‐life respiratory infections. This systematic review and meta‐analysis compared the cell types involved in airways inflammation in children with and without RSV, noting that immune responses can influence long‐term complications and may involve different inflammatory cells. Method We searched for relevant studies published in English on PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar and Web of Science until 31 August 2025. Bias assessment was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Heatmaps were generated and forest plots were created, with I 2 values over 40% indicating heterogeneity. Results The search identified 126 studies and a quantitative meta‐analysis was conducted on six studies that comprised 202 with RSV and 97 unaffected controls. Compared to the controls, children with RSV showed increased percentages of neutrophils and decreased macrophages in their bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Forest plots revealed that the pooled standard mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for neutrophil and macrophage percentages were 2.12 (1.74 to 2.50) and −3.14 (−4.16 to −2.12), respectively. Conclusion Overall, this systematic review and meta‐analysis suggested that neutrophils predominated in the airways of children with RSV. This highlights the value of investigating these in future studies.

title: Bivalent RSVpreF Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)-Related Respiratory Disease Hospitalization and Emergency Department Visits Across Three RSV Seasons.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) protein subunit vaccines reduce the risk of severe outcomes such as hospitalization and emergency department (ED) visits for at least two RSV seasons following vaccination. No data have been published on real-world RSV vaccine effectiveness (VE) beyond the second season after vaccination. This study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE against RSV-related respiratory disease hospitalizations/ED visits throughout three seasons after vaccination. METHODS: This retrospective test-negative case-control study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE among adults aged ≥60 years at Kaiser Permanente Southern California, USA, with lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) or acute respiratory illness (ARI) over three RSV seasons (11/24/2023-4/18/2026). Cases were RSV-positive without coinfection. Controls were negative for RSV, hMPV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and positive for a non-vaccine preventable disease pathogen. Exposure was bivalent RSVpreF (Abrysvo) receipt ≥ 21 days before LRTD/ARI. Adjusted VE was estimated using odds ratios from multivariable logistic regression or generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related LRTD hospitalization/ED visits was 80% (95% CI 68-87), 70% (95% CI 53-81), and 51% (95% CI -12-78) in the first, second, and third season after vaccination, respectively. Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related ARI hospitalization/ED visits was 81% (71-87), 64% (48-75), and 60% (15-81), respectively. Adjusted VE among non-immunocompromised individuals trended 4-7% higher than corresponding overall estimates. Overall adjusted VE across the three combined seasons was 73% (95% CI 64-80) and 73% (95% CI 65-79) against RSV-related LRTD and ARI, respectively. CONCLUSION: Bivalent RSVpreF provides protection against RSV-related respiratory hospitalization/ED visits for at least three seasons after vaccination in this population of older adults with a high prevalence of comorbidities. Estimates in the third season for ARI were more definitive, while those for LRTD were imprecise due to limited event numbers. This suggests bivalent RSVpreF vaccination results in substantial individual and public health benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06077968.

source_records.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) protein subunit vaccines reduce the risk of severe outcomes such as hospitalization and emergency department (ED) visits for at least two RSV seasons following vaccination. No data have been published on real-world RSV vaccine effectiveness (VE) beyond the second season after vaccination. This study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE against RSV-related respiratory disease hospitalizations/ED visits throughout three seasons after vaccination. METHODS: This retrospective test-negative case-control study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE among adults aged ≥60 years at Kaiser Permanente Southern California, USA, with lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) or acute respiratory illness (ARI) over three RSV seasons (11/24/2023-4/18/2026). Estimates in the third season for ARI were more definitive, while those for LRTD were imprecise due to limited event numbers. This suggests bivalent RSVpreF vaccination results in substantial individual and public health benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06077968.

title: Burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalizations among adults aged 60 years or more in Brazil: A retrospective surveillance database analysis (2013-2024).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Globally, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in adults aged ≥60 years. Risk increases with advancing age and comorbidities, particularly cardiopulmonary disease and diabetes. RSV disease burden in adults is often underestimated due to non-specific presentation and limited testing. In Brazil, RSV is a recognized driver of hospitalizations and deaths in older adults, yet comprehensive epidemiological data remain scarce. Here, we describe RSV-associated severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospitalizations among adults aged ≥60 years in Brazil between 2013 and 2024. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed RSV-associated SARI hospitalizations reported to the national Influenza Epidemiological Surveillance Information System -Gripe. Outcomes included hospitalization frequency, in-hospital mortality, case fatality rates (CFRs), seasonality, healthcare resource utilization, and comorbidities. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2024, 4,636 RSV-related hospitalizations occurred in adults aged ≥60 years, increasing sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2024). Hospitalization rates increased from 15 per 100,000 in 2024. Women accounted for most cases (59%), and hospitalizations were concentrated in the South and Southeast regions partly due to test availability. In-hospital mortality increased over time, with mean rates nearly fivefold higher post-pandemic than pre-pandemic. CFRs remained consistently high (21-31%), particularly in adults aged ≥80 years. The mean length of hospital stay was 12.9 days. Almost one-third of cases required intensive care unit admission, of whom more than two-thirds needed ventilatory support. Comorbidities were present in 71% of cases, most commonly cardiovascular (65%) and diabetes (33%)were strongly associated with increased mortality and healthcare resource utilization. CONCLUSIONS: RSV poses a substantial and increasing burden among Brazilian adults aged ≥60 years, with a high CFR, prolonged hospitalizations, and intensive healthcare resource utilization. These findings highlight the need to strengthen RSV surveillance and discuss vaccination strategies for adults aged older in Brazil.

title: Bardoxolone methyl exerts an inhibitory effect on respiratory syncytial virus infection by downregulating IL-6 via the IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway.
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, but therapeutic options for active infection remain limited. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) contributes to RSV replication and RSV-induced inflammation, and the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway is a major regulator of IL-6 expression. Bardoxolone methyl (BXM) was identified by network medicine as a potential anti-RSV compound, with molecular docking suggesting interactions with the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. We investigated whether BXM inhibits RSV infection through modulation of the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in RSV-infected BEAS-2B cells and BALB/c mice. RSV infection increased IL-6 expression and activated IKKβ/NF-κB signaling, whereas IL-6 knockdown reduced viral replication and inflammatory mediator expression. BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication, as shown by RT-qPCR, TCID50, plaque reduction assays, and Western blotting, and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro . Mechanistically, BXM attenuated RSV-induced phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB. The IKKβ inhibitor TPCA-1 produced similar inhibitory effects, whereas recombinant human IL-6 add-back partially restored inflammatory mediator expression in BXM-treated RSV-infected cells. In mice, BXM reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury. These findings suggest that BXM suppresses RSV replication and inflammation, at least in part, by modulating the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for RSV infection. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Although preventive strategies are available for some high-risk groups, treatment options for active RSV infection remain limited. This study identifies bardoxolone methyl (BXM) as a potential anti-RSV compound and shows that it can reduce both viral replication and virus-induced inflammation in cell and mouse models. Importantly, our findings suggest that BXM acts, at least in part, by reducing IL-6-related inflammatory signaling, which is closely associated with RSV disease severity. These results provide experimental evidence supporting BXM as a promising candidate for further development against RSV infection and offer insight into a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy.

abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)会导致婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群的严重下呼吸道感染,但针对活动性感染的治疗选择仍然有限。白细胞介素-6(IL-6)促进RSV复制和RSV引发的炎症,而IKKβ/NF-κB通路是调控IL-6表达的主要途径。甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)通过网络医学被鉴定为一种潜在的抗RSV化合物,分子对接研究表明其与IKKβ/NF-κB通路存在相互作用。我们研究了BXM是否通过调节RSV感染的BEAS-2B细胞和BALB/c小鼠中的IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴来抑制RSV感染。RSV感染会增加IL-6表达并激活IKKβ/NF-κB信号通路,而IL-6敲低则会减少病毒复制和炎症介质的表达。BXM在体外显著抑制了RSV复制,如RT-qPCR、TCID50、斑块减少实验和Western blotting所示,并降低了IL-6的表达。从机制上看,BXM减弱了RSV诱导的IKKβ和NF-κB的磷酸化。IKKβ抑制剂TPCA-1产生了类似的抑制效果,而重组人IL-6添加则部分恢复了BXM处理的RSV感染细胞中炎症介质的表达。在小鼠中,BXM降低了肺部病毒滴度、RSV-F表达、IL-6表达、IKKβ/NF-κB激活以及RSV诱导的肺损伤。这些发现表明,BXM通过调节IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴抑制RSV复制和炎症,支持其作为RSV感染治疗候选药物的潜力。重要性 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致呼吸道疾病的主要原因之一,尤其是在婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群中。尽管某些高危群体已有预防策略,但针对活动性RSV感染的治疗选择仍然有限。本研究确定了甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)作为潜在的抗RSV化合物,并表明其在细胞和小鼠模型中可以减少病毒复制和病毒诱导的炎症。重要的是,我们的发现表明,BXM至少部分通过减少与IL-6相关的炎症信号发挥作用,而这些信号与RSV疾病的严重程度密切相关。这些结果为BXM作为对抗RSV感染的潜在候选药物提供了实验依据,并为针对宿主的治疗策略提供了见解。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,BXM通过调节IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴抑制RSV复制和炎症,支持其作为RSV感染治疗候选药物的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为BXM作为对抗RSV感染的潜在候选药物提供了实验依据,并为针对宿主的治疗策略提供了见解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了体外实验和动物模型,这些可能无法完全代表人类RSV感染。由于缺乏临床试验数据,证据强度中等。

title: Molecular detection of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized children at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo
abstract: Epidemiological Respiratory viral infections are among the most common diseases responsible for morbidity and mortality among children in sub-Saharan Africa, with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) being a major contributor. This situation highlights the urgent need for rapid and accurate diagnostic tools. The objective of this study was to detect RSV among hospitalized children under five years of age with acute respiratory infections at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville in the Republic of the Congo. A total of 81 nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from children aged ≤5 years who were admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit and Neonatology Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville with acute respiratory infections between August and December 2023. Respiratory viruses were identified using rapid antigen detection assays and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Rapid antigen tests detected SARS-CoV-2 in 2 cases (2.5%), whereas RSV and influenza A and B were not detected. In contrast, RT-qPCR identified RSV in 4 samples (4.9%). All RSV-positive patients were male, aged over 28 days, and hospitalized in the pediatric intensive care unit. The main clinical signs observed were respiratory distress (100%), cough (75%), fever (50%) and rhinorrhea (50%). These findings confirm the circulation of RSV among hospitalized children at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville and highlight the superior sensitivity of RT-qPCR over rapid antigen tests for RSV detection. Key words: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), children, rapid antigen test, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Brazzaville.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to detect respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among hospitalized children under five years of age with acute respiratory infections at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville in the Republic of the Congo. The researchers used rapid antigen detection assays and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) to identify respiratory viruses. While rapid antigen tests did not detect RSV, RT-qPCR identified it in 4 samples (4.9%). These findings confirm the circulation of RSV in the region and emphasize the superior sensitivity of RT-qPCR for RSV detection. The study highlights the need for more accurate diagnostic tools in sub-Saharan Africa to address the burden of respiratory infections in children. However, the study was limited to a single hospital and a specific time period, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the limited sample size and geographic focus.

title_zh: 刚果共和国布拉扎维尔大学医院中心住院儿童中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的分子检测
source_body_en: Epidemiological Respiratory viral infections are among the most common diseases responsible for morbidity and mortality among children in sub-Saharan Africa, with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) being a major contributor. This situation highlights the urgent need for rapid and accurate diagnostic tools. The objective of this study was to detect RSV among hospitalized children under five years of age with acute respiratory infections at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville in the Republic of the Congo. A total of 81 nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from children aged ≤5 years who were admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit and Neonatology Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville with acute respiratory infections between August and December 2023. Respiratory viruses were identified using rapid antigen detection assays and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Rapid antigen tests detected SARS-CoV-2 in 2 cases (2.5%), whereas RSV and influenza A and B were not detected. In contrast, RT-qPCR identified RSV in 4 samples (4.9%). All RSV-positive patients were male, aged over 28 days, and hospitalized in the pediatric intensive care unit. The main clinical signs observed were respiratory distress (100%), cough (75%), fever (50%) and rhinorrhea (50%). These findings confirm the circulation of RSV among hospitalized children at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville and highlight the superior sensitivity of RT-qPCR over rapid antigen tests for RSV detection. Key words: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), children, rapid antigen test, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Brazzaville.
abstract_zh: 流行病学呼吸道病毒感染是撒哈拉以南非洲儿童发病率和死亡率的主要原因之一,其中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是主要贡献者。这一情况凸显了快速准确诊断工具的迫切需求。本研究的目的是检测刚果共和国布拉扎维尔大学医院中心住院的5岁以下急性呼吸道感染儿童中的RSV。2023年8月至12月期间,从布拉扎维尔大学医院中心儿科重症监护室和新生儿科收治的年龄≤5岁的儿童中收集了81份鼻咽拭子样本。使用快速抗原检测试验和逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)鉴定呼吸道病毒。快速抗原检测试验在2例(2.5%)中检测到SARS-CoV-2,而RSV和流感A、B型病毒均未被检测到。相比之下,RT-qPCR在4份样本(4.9%)中检测到RSV。所有RSV阳性患者均为男性,年龄超过28天,并住院在儿科重症监护室。观察到的主要临床症状包括呼吸窘迫(100%)、咳嗽(75%)、发热(50%)和流涕(50%)。这些发现证实了RSV在刚果共和国布拉扎维尔大学医院中心住院儿童中的流行,并突显了RT-qPCR在RSV检测中相较于快速抗原检测试验的更高灵敏度。关键词:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、儿童、快速抗原检测、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)、布拉扎维尔。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

title: Post-pandemic re-establishment of respiratory virus seasonality and molecular epidemiology of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus in Northern Italy: a three-year surveillance study (2023-2026).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited. METHODS: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital. Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing. RESULTS: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases. CONCLUSIONS: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS INFECTION IN PATIENTS WITH RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS: DOES DISEASE STATUS AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSION ALTER CLINICAL COURSE, SEVERITY, AND HOSPITALIZATION RISK?
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an increasingly recognized cause of severe respiratory infection in older adults, particularly those with underlying comorbidities and immunosuppression. However, the specific burden of RSV disease in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) remains incompletely characterized. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology in immunocompromised populations, pathophysiological mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility in RA, risk stratification approaches, clinical presentation and complications, prevention strategies including recently approved vaccines (Arexvy, Abrysvo, mResvia), and clinical management recommendations. Recent data demonstrate that RA patients have substantially higher hospitalization rates (approximately 54%) compared with immunocompetent older adults (6–8%), with frailty emerging as the strongest independent predictor of severe infection (adjusted odds ratio 5.15). Contemporary evidence supports the benefit of RSV vaccination in older adults; however, reduced immunogenicity has been documented in patients receiving targeted immunosuppressive therapies. This review emphasizes individualized risk assessment, optimization of immunosuppression, timely vaccination with enhanced monitoring in high-risk subgroups, early clinical recognition of RSV infection, and evidence-based management approaches. By integrating clinical epidemiology with preventive and therapeutic strategies, contemporary practice can substantially reduce RSV-related complications in this vulnerable population.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是老年人群中日益被认可的严重呼吸道感染原因之一,尤其是那些有基础合并症和免疫抑制的患者。然而,RSV感染在类风湿关节炎(RA)和其他系统性自身免疫风湿性疾病(SARD)患者中的具体负担仍不完全明确。本叙述性综述综合了当前关于RSV在免疫缺陷人群中感染的证据,探讨了RA患者中增加易感性的病理生理机制,风险分层方法,临床表现和并发症,预防策略包括最近获批的尼塞韦单抗(Arexvy,Abrysvo,mResvia),以及临床管理建议。最新数据显示,RA患者RSV感染的住院率显著高于免疫功能正常的老年人(约54% vs 6–8%),而虚弱是严重感染最强的独立预测因素(调整比值比5.15)。当前证据支持在老年人群中使用RSV疫苗的益处;然而,在接受靶向免疫抑制治疗的患者中,已记录到疫苗免疫原性降低的现象。本综述强调个体化风险评估、免疫抑制优化、在高风险亚组中及时接种疫苗并加强监测、早期识别RSV感染以及基于证据的管理方法。通过将临床数据与预防和治疗策略相结合,现代实践可以显著减少这一易感人群的RSV相关并发症。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于类风湿关节炎(RA)患者中的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染,探讨疾病状态和免疫抑制是否改变临床过程、严重程度和住院风险。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是对当前关于RSV在免疫缺陷人群中感染的证据进行叙述性综合,涵盖病理生理机制、风险分层、临床表现、预防策略和管理建议。它未报告特定数据库、检索日期或荟萃分析方法。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,RSV疾病在RA患者中的具体负担仍不完全明确。缺乏关于RSV疫苗在RA患者中有效性以及该人群RSV易感性增加的精确机制的详细数据。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness Among US Older Adults, 2023-2024 Season
abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes a substantial number of hospitalizations and deaths among older adults. Two RSV vaccines for individuals aged 60 years or older were approved in 2023; it was important to monitor their clinical effectiveness during routine care in the first RSV season after regulatory approval. Objective: To estimate the clinical effectiveness of RSV vaccines during routine care overall and by brand among US older adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This nationally representative, retrospective cohort study evaluated the effectiveness of RSV vaccines from August 6, 2023, to March 2, 2024. The primary analysis included eligible Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries aged 65 years or older. Exposures: The RSVPreF3+AS01 RSV vaccine (GSK) and RSVpreF RSV vaccine (Pfizer). Main Outcomes and Measures: RSV-related hospitalization and RSV-related death. Results: Among 14 819 226 unvaccinated beneficiaries at the beginning of the study, the median age was 74 years (IQR, 70-79 years) and 57.7% were female. By the study end date, 13.9% of beneficiaries had received a RSVPreF3+AS01 vaccine, and 6.4% received a RSVpreF vaccine. Compared with the unvaccinated cohort, vaccinated individuals were less likely to have low-income status, lived in more affluent areas, and were more likely to have prior influenza vaccination and prior COVID-19 vaccination. The RSVPreF3+AS01 and RSVpreF vaccinated cohorts were largely comparable in demographic, social, and medical characteristics. Overall estimated vaccine effectiveness compared with the unvaccinated cohort was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.0%-83.4%) against RSV-related hospitalization and 85.0% (95% CI, 75.1%-90.9%) against RSV-related death. Brand-specific vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 79.9% (95% CI, 77.6%-81.9%) for RSVPreF3+AS01 and 85.1% (95% CI, 82.2%-87.5%) for RSVpreF compared with the unvaccinated cohort. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 72.2% (95% CI, 67.4%-76.3%) for immunocompromised individuals. Effectiveness did not change significantly with age. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cohort study of US older adults, both RSVPreF3+AS01 and RSVpreF vaccines had high effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization and death during the 2023-2024 season. RSV vaccines demonstrated substantial effectiveness within this high-risk older adult population, including among immunocompromised individuals and across all ages 65 years or older. This large postmarketing noninterventional study provides clinical evidence of RSV vaccine effectiveness in the first year of vaccine approval.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness of two RSV vaccines, RSVPreF3+AS01 (GSK) and RSVpreF (Pfizer), among US older adults during the 2023-2024 season. The research is motivated by the significant burden of RSV-related hospitalizations and deaths in this population and the need to monitor vaccine performance post-approval. A nationally representative, retrospective cohort study design was used, analyzing Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries aged 65 years or older. The study found that overall vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.0%-83.4%) and against RSV-related death was 85.0% (95% CI, 75.1%-90.9%). Brand-specific effectiveness was 79.9% (95% CI, 77.6%-81.9%) for RSVPreF3+AS01 and 85.1% (95% CI, 82.2%-87.5%) for RSVpreF. Immunocompromised individuals showed 72.2% (95% CI, 67.4%-76.3%) effectiveness against hospitalization, and effectiveness did not vary significantly with age. The study highlights the substantial effectiveness of RSV vaccines in older adults, including those at higher risk, and provides important postmarketing evidence for vaccine use. However, the retrospective design may introduce biases, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 重要性:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)导致大量老年人住院和死亡。2023年,针对60岁及以上人群的两种RSV疫苗获批;在监管批准后的首个RSV季节中,监测其在常规医疗护理中的临床有效性至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项具有全国代表性的回顾性研究评估了2023年8月6日至2024年3月2日期间RSV疫苗的有效性。主要分析包括符合资格的65岁及以上Medicare按服务收费受益人。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用回顾性研究设计,通过比较接种和未接种RSV疫苗的受益人来估计RSV疫苗的有效性。暴露因素定义为接种RSVPreF3+AS01或RSVpreF疫苗,主要结果为RSV相关住院和RSV相关死亡。
elements_zh.main_results: 在研究开始时,共有14,819,226名未接种疫苗的受益人,中位年龄为74岁(四分位距,70-79岁),其中57.7%为女性。截至研究结束日期,13.9%的受益人接种了RSVPreF3+AS01疫苗,6.4%接种了RSVpreF疫苗。与未接种疫苗的受益人相比,总体估计的RSV疫苗有效性为:对RSV相关住院的有效性为81.8%(95%置信区间,80.0%-83.4%),对RSV相关死亡的有效性为85.0%(95%置信区间,75.1%-90.9%)。针对RSV相关住院的品牌特定有效性分别为:RSVPreF3+AS01为79.9%(95%置信区间,77.6%-81.9%),RSVpreF为85.1%(95%置信区间,82.2%-87.5%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了RSV疫苗在获批后的第一年中的临床有效性证据。RSV疫苗在这一高风险老年群体中显示出显著的有效性,包括免疫功能低下个体和所有65岁及以上年龄层。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解RSV疫苗在老年人中的临床有效性提供了信息,这对公共卫生规划和疫苗实施策略至关重要。这项大规模上市后的非干预性研究为了解RSV疫苗在获批后的首个季节中的影响提供了宝贵的数据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项回顾性研究,可能受到偏倚和混杂因素的影响。然而,大样本量和全国代表性设计为研究结果提供了中等程度的信心。

title: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine impact over three respiratory syncytial virus seasons in older adults with comorbidities.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We explored the efficacy of AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) in subpopulations of participants with underlying medical conditions in the multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial (conducted between May 2021 and May 2024). METHODS: Medically stable ≥60-year-olds were 1:1-randomised to receive one adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo dose pre-RSV season 1. In exploratory post hoc analyses in subgroups of participants with underlying conditions (including COPD, asthma, diabetes and obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg·m-2)), we evaluated efficacy of one vaccine dose against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD), RSV-related acute respiratory illness (RSV-ARI) and RSV-ARI-related complications (e.g., pneumonia, COPD/asthma exacerbation and cardiovascular events). We also evaluated (post hoc) RSV-ARI-related systemic corticosteroid and antibiotics use in participants with COPD or asthma. RESULTS: The efficacy analyses comprised 12 468 vaccine and 12 498 placebo recipients. Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar among participants with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1) and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8). Efficacy was also observed against RSV-ARI in these subgroups. Efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications was 74.4% (95% CI: 11.2-95.2) in participants with COPD and 60.8% (-9.9-88.7) in those with asthma. Among participants with COPD, 15.4% (1.9-45.4) of RSV-ARI episodes in vaccine versus 22.4% (12.5-35.3) in placebo recipients were treated with systemic corticosteroids, and 46.2% (19.2-74.9) versus 56.9% (43.2-69.8) with antibiotics. CONCLUSIONS: Post hoc analyses of the AReSVi-006 trial suggest that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions like COPD and asthma.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in older adults with comorbidities during three RSV seasons, addressing the need for targeted prevention strategies in high-risk populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial conducted between May 2021 and May 2024, randomising medically stable ≥60-year-olds in a 1:1 ratio to receive one dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo pre-RSV season.
analysis.methods: Participants were randomised to receive one dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo, and post hoc analyses were conducted to assess vaccine efficacy against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease, RSV-related acute respiratory illness, and related complications in subgroups with underlying conditions such as COPD, asthma, diabetes, and obesity.
analysis.main_results: Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar across subgroups with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1), and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine may be effective in preventing RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD, and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide evidence for the potential use of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in preventing RSV-related illnesses in high-risk older adults, which could inform future vaccination strategies for this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on post hoc analyses, which may introduce bias, and the efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications showed wide confidence intervals, suggesting moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in older adults with comorbidities during three RSV seasons. The multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial randomised medically stable participants aged ≥60 years to receive one dose of the vaccine or placebo. Post hoc analyses showed similar efficacy against RSV-LRTD across subgroups with COPD, asthma, diabetes, and obesity as in the overall population. Efficacy against RSV-ARI was also observed in these subgroups. The study suggests the vaccine may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD, and related complications in high-risk older adults. However, the findings are based on post hoc analyses, which may introduce bias, and the confidence intervals for efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications were wide, indicating moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.methods: 参与者被随机分配接受一剂佐剂修饰的RSVPreF3或安慰剂,并进行了事后分析,以评估疫苗在具有基础疾病(如慢性阻塞性肺疾病、哮喘、糖尿病和肥胖)的亚群中对RSV相关下呼吸道疾病、RSV相关急性呼吸道疾病及其相关并发症的有效性。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为佐剂修饰的RSVPreF3 疫苗在高风险老年群体中预防RSV相关疾病的应用提供了证据,可能有助于未来针对该人群的疫苗接种策略制定。

Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar among participants with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1) and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8). Efficacy was also observed against RSV-ARI in these subgroups. Efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications was 74.4% (95% CI: 11.2-95.2) in participants with COPD and 60.8% (-9.9-88.7) in those with asthma. Among participants with COPD, 15.4% (1.9-45.4) of RSV-ARI episodes in vaccine versus 22.4% (12.5-35.3) in placebo recipients were treated with systemic corticosteroids, and 46.2% (19.2-74.9) versus 56.9% (43.2-69.8) with antibiotics. CONCLUSIONS: Post hoc analyses of the AReSVi-006 trial suggest that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions like COPD and asthma.

analysis_zh.methods: 参与者被随机分配接受一剂佐剂修饰的RSVPreF3或安慰剂,并进行了事后分析,以评估疫苗在具有基础疾病(如慢性阻塞性肺疾病、哮喘、糖尿病和肥胖)的亚群中对RSV相关下呼吸道疾病、RSV相关急性呼吸道疾病及其相关并发症的有效性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,佐剂修饰的RSVPreF3 疫苗可能在医疗稳定的有基础疾病的老年群体中有效预防RSV-ARI、RSV-LRTD以及RSV相关并发症。

title: Viral Metagenomic Sequencing Reveals Viral Codetection Patterns in Children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections, yet the frequency and composition of viral codetections in affected children have not been extensively profiled using unbiased sequencing approaches. Here, we performed viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs collected from 42 pediatric patients with confirmed RSV infection to characterize the codetection landscape. RSV was detected and genotyped in all specimens. Beyond RSV, we identified nine additional human respiratory viruses coexisting across the cohort; several of these fall outside the scope of routine diagnostic panels, although their clinical significance remains uncertain. Codetections were the rule rather than the exception: 30 of 42 samples harbored at least three viruses, with up to seven distinct viruses detected in a single case. These findings underscore the taxonomic breadth and polymicrobial complexity of respiratory infections in children. Our results describe the viral codetection landscape in RSV-infected children, revealing a broader spectrum of co-occurring viruses than typically captured by targeted diagnostics, although the clinical significance of most codetections remains uncertain. These findings highlight the polymicrobial complexity of RSV infections and underscore the need for prospective studies to determine which codetections are clinically meaningful.

title: Characteristics and outcomes of adult patients hospitalised with RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 in Belgium, winter seasons 2023/24 and 2024/25
abstract: BACKGROUND Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) cause substantial disease burden in older adults and those with comorbidities. AIM To inform Belgian vaccination policies, we aimed to compare risk profiles and outcomes of influenza, COVID-19 and RSV infections and examine age-related differences. METHODS Adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalised with SARI in nine Belgian sentinel hospitals during the 2023/24 and 2024/25 winter seasons were included. Patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 were compared in terms of demographics, comorbidities, complications and outcomes. Adults 18–64 years were compared with those ≥ 65 years. Multivariate analyses were applied. RESULTS Among 2,806 patients, 535 (19.1%) had RSV infection, 1,694 (60.4%) influenza and 577 (20.6%) COVID-19. Patients with influenza were significantly younger (mean age 68.9 years) and had significantly fewer comorbidities (89.7%) than patients with RSV (73.8 years; 95.8%) or COVID-19 (74.0 years; 93.6%). Patients with COVID-19 experienced significantly fewer complications (40.8%) than patients with RSV (48.9%) or influenza (45.2%). Patients with RSV had higher in-hospital mortality (11.9%) than patients with influenza (7.3%; p = 0.089) or COVID-19 (6.9%; p = 0.037). Across pathogens, younger adults had relatively more comorbidities after adjusting for differences in the general population. They had shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, but higher intensive care unit admission rates. CONCLUSION Patients with RSV infection had a disease course comparable to patients with influenza or COVID-19 and a higher mortality rate, especially with increasing age. These findings highlight the importance of RSV vaccination in older adults and those with comorbidities, alongside established vaccination strategies for seasonal influenza and COVID-19.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to compare the risk profiles and outcomes of RSV, influenza, and COVID-19 infections in adults hospitalised in Belgium during the winter seasons of 2023/24 and 2024/25. It included 2,806 patients, with 535 having RSV infection, 1,694 influenza, and 577 COVID-19. The study found that patients with RSV were significantly older and had more comorbidities than those with influenza or COVID-19. RSV infection was associated with higher in-hospital mortality compared to both influenza and COVID-19. The results suggest that RSV vaccination should be prioritised for older adults and those with comorbidities, similar to current strategies for influenza and COVID-19. The study used multivariate analyses to compare age-related differences, but it does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

title: Development and application of nbLIBRA-seq for high-throughput discovery of antigen-specific nanobodies.
abstract: Nanobodies are of high interest in many fields of medicine and biotechnology, although nanobody discovery has been limited by laborious screening techniques. Here, we demonstrate the successful adaptation of linking B cell receptor to antigen specificity through sequencing (LIBRA-seq) to immunized alpacas for the rapid identification of antigen-specific nanobodies, derived from heavy-chain antibodies. We validated LIBRA-seq for nanobody discovery (nbLIBRA-seq) in two different disease settings. First, we identified over 300 antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies against human transferrin receptor (TfR1) from a single alpaca blood sample. Second, we tested the efficiency of nbLIBRA-seq with multiple antigens in the screening library. Using fusion glycoproteins from the related respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), 1,125 antigen-specific heavy-chain-expressing B cells were recovered. Our results illustrate the potential of nbLIBRA-seq to rapidly identify antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies for a range of diverse targets, a capability that will be critical for the efficient development of nanobody-based therapeutics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of traditional nanobody discovery methods by developing a high-throughput approach for identifying antigen-specific nanobodies, particularly in the context of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved validating the nbLIBRA-seq method in two different disease settings, focusing on the identification of antigen-specific nanobodies against RSV and other related pathogens.
analysis.methods: The researchers adapted the LIBRA-seq technique to immunized alpacas, using fusion glycoproteins from RSV and human metapneumovirus to screen for antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies.
analysis.main_results: Over 300 antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies against human transferrin receptor (TfR1) were identified from a single alpaca blood sample, and 1,125 antigen-specific heavy-chain-expressing B cells were recovered using RSV and human metapneumovirus fusion glycoproteins.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate that nbLIBRA-seq can efficiently identify antigen-specific nanobodies, offering a significant advancement in the development of nanobody-based therapeutics for RSV and related targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that nbLIBRA-seq could enhance the rapid discovery of nanobodies for RSV and other related viruses, potentially accelerating the development of targeted therapeutics and improving public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level reporting and does not provide detailed statistical analyses or long-term efficacy data, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces nbLIBRA-seq, a high-throughput method for identifying antigen-specific nanobodies, with a focus on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The researchers validated the technique in two disease settings, demonstrating its ability to rapidly discover nanobodies against RSV and human metapneumovirus. The results highlight the potential of nbLIBRA-seq to improve the development of nanobody-based therapeutics for RSV-related diseases. However, the study is limited to abstract-level reporting and lacks detailed statistical or long-term efficacy data, which may affect the strength of the evidence. The findings could have significant implications for the efficient discovery of nanobodies against RSV and related pathogens, supporting future research and public health applications.

title_zh: nbLIBRA-seq技术的开发与应用:用于高通量发现抗原特异性纳米抗体
source_body_en: Nanobodies are of high interest in many fields of medicine and biotechnology, although nanobody discovery has been limited by laborious screening techniques. Here, we demonstrate the successful adaptation of linking B cell receptor to antigen specificity through sequencing (LIBRA-seq) to immunized alpacas for the rapid identification of antigen-specific nanobodies, derived from heavy-chain antibodies. We validated LIBRA-seq for nanobody discovery (nbLIBRA-seq) in two different disease settings. First, we identified over 300 antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies against human transferrin receptor (TfR1) from a single alpaca blood sample. Second, we tested the efficiency of nbLIBRA-seq with multiple antigens in the screening library. Using fusion glycoproteins from the related respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), 1,125 antigen-specific heavy-chain-expressing B cells were recovered. Our results illustrate the potential of nbLIBRA-seq to rapidly identify antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies for a range of diverse targets, a capability that will be critical for the efficient development of nanobody-based therapeutics.
abstract_zh: 纳米抗体在医学和生物技术的许多领域都备受关注,尽管纳米抗体的发现一直受到繁琐筛选技术的限制。在这里,我们展示了将B细胞受体与抗原特异性通过测序连接(LIBRA-seq)技术成功应用于免疫骆驼,以快速鉴定来源于重链抗体的抗原特异性纳米抗体。我们在两种不同的疾病背景下验证了用于纳米抗体发现的LIBRA-seq技术(nbLIBRA-seq)。首先,我们从单个骆驼血液样本中鉴定了超过300种针对人类转铁蛋白受体(TfR1)的抗原特异性重链抗体。其次,我们使用与呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人类副流感病毒(hMPV)相关的融合糖蛋白,测试了nbLIBRA-seq在筛选库中的效率,成功回收了1,125个抗原特异性重链表达的B细胞。我们的结果展示了nbLIBRA-seq在快速鉴定针对多种不同靶标的抗原特异性重链抗体方面的潜力,这一能力对于高效开发基于纳米抗体的治疗药物至关重要。

title: Human metapneumovirus in central China, 2024–2025: epidemiology, co-infections, and temporal dynamics
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections in children, but comprehensive data from sentinel surveillance in the post‐pandemic period remain limited. Understanding its epidemiology and co‐infection patterns is critical for surveillance and prevention. We analyzed 36,143 respiratory specimens from ILI/SARI patients in Henan, China (2024–2025) using multiplex PCR for HMPV and 14 other pathogens. Positivity rates, enrichment ratios, co‐infection patterns, pathogen associations (OR/PR), and temporal dynamics (cross‐correlation and regression) were assessed. Overall HMPV positivity was 3.96% (1,432/36,143), with a sharp inter-year difference: 7.1% in 2024 vs. 1.7% in 2025, peaking at 26.2% during week 48. Children aged 3–5 years had the highest positivity (8.6%; enrichment ratio 2.18). Co-infections occurred in 56.2% of HMPV-positive cases, predominantly with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. HMPV showed positive associations with these bacteria (OR = 2.01 and 1.47, respectively) but negative associations with influenza virus (OR = 0.20) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (OR = 0.17). HBoV also showed a positive association (OR = 1.66). RSV positivity at a 1-week lag had a positive effect on HMPV (β = 0.15, P = 0.048). HMPV was frequently detected in pediatric ILI/SARI patients during 2024–2025, with high rates of bacterial co‐detection. The temporal lead‐lag relationship with RSV underscores the need for integrated surveillance and age‐targeted prevention. The marked 2024 resurgence warrants continued monitoring to determine whether the observed patterns represent a short‐term anomaly or a sustained change in HMPV circulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the epidemiology of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in Henan, China, during 2024–2025, focusing on its co-infection patterns and temporal dynamics. The research aimed to fill knowledge gaps regarding HMPV's role in respiratory infections post-pandemic. Using multiplex PCR, the study analyzed 36,143 respiratory specimens from ILI/SARI patients, revealing an overall positivity rate of 3.96% with a notable inter-year variation. Children aged 3–5 years showed the highest HMPV positivity, and co-infections were common, particularly with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. HMPV was positively associated with HBoV and RSV at a 1-week lag, but negatively associated with influenza virus and RSV. These findings emphasize the need for integrated surveillance and age-specific prevention strategies, though the study's geographic limitation and reliance on sentinel data suggest moderate evidence strength.

abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是儿童急性呼吸道感染的主要原因之一,但疫情后哨点监测的综合数据仍较为有限。了解其流行病学及共感染模式对于监测和预防至关重要。我们对2024–2025年中国河南省ILI/SARI患者的36,143份呼吸道样本进行了多重PCR检测,以识别HMPV及其他14种病原体。评估了阳性率、富集比、共感染模式、病原体关联性(OR/PR)以及时间动态(交叉相关性和回归分析)。总体HMPV阳性率为3.96%(1,432/36,143),且年际差异显著:2024年为7.1%,2025年为1.7%,在第48周达到峰值26.2%。3–5岁儿童的阳性率最高(8.6%;富集比2.18)。HMPV阳性病例中56.2%发生了共感染,主要与肺炎链球菌和流感嗜血杆菌相关。HMPV与这些细菌呈正相关(OR分别为2.01和1.47),但与流感病毒(OR = 0.20)和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV,OR = 0.17)呈负相关。HMPV还与人类博卡病毒(HBoV)呈正相关(OR = 1.66)。RSV在1周滞后时的阳性率对HMPV有正向影响(β = 0.15,P = 0.048)。2024–2025年期间,HMPV在儿科ILI/SARI患者中频繁检出,且细菌共感染率较高。与RSV的时间领先滞后关系表明需要整合监测并针对年龄制定预防策略。2024年的显著回升提示应持续监测,以确定所观察到的模式是短期异常还是HMPV传播的持续变化。

title: Computational designing of multiepitope based vaccine (MEBV) candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV) using immunoinformatics approach
abstract: Abstract Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a paramyxoviridae family respiratory pathogen, which is closely related to respiratory syncytial virus. It produces the symptoms of the flu and it may result in the serious damage of the airways and even though it is a worldwide problem, there is no vaccine available as yet. Three antigenic proteins namely surface glycoprotein, nucleoprotein and phosphoprotein were screened from all the receptors and showed no similarity to host genome. The three viral proteins were then screened for identifying the cytotoxic and helper T cell lymphocytes as well as linear and conformational B-cell lymphocytes. The vaccine had 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, which were combined with linkers and beta-defensin as adjuvant into a 296-amino-acid MEBV with antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed that there is a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of − 14.6 and immune activation. Moreover, the disulfide engineering enhanced construct stability. Cloning and codon optimization was used to verify efficient expression in the target host. Taken together, these findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen of HMPV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to design a multiepitope vaccine candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV) due to its role as a respiratory pathogen closely related to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), which lacks an available vaccine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved computational designing of a multiepitope vaccine (MEBV) candidate against HMPV, using immunoinformatics methods to identify potential epitopes and assess vaccine properties.
analysis.methods: The researchers used computational tools to screen three viral proteins for epitopes, combined them with linkers and beta-defensin as an adjuvant, and performed molecular docking and MD simulations to evaluate interactions with human TLR3.
analysis.main_results: The MEBV candidate was composed of 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, resulting in a 296-amino-acid construct with an antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of −14.6.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen for HMPV, offering a novel approach to vaccine development against this virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into HMPV vaccine development, which could improve surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for HMPV-related respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which limits the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a computational approach to designing a multiepitope vaccine (MEBV) candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV), a respiratory pathogen closely related to RSV. The researchers identified three viral proteins with no similarity to the host genome and selected epitopes for MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell recognition. The MEBV construct, containing 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, was evaluated for antigenicity and interaction with human TLR3, showing a binding energy of −14.6. The findings suggest the MEBV has potential as an immunogen for HMPV, offering a novel vaccine design strategy. However, the study is limited to computational methods without experimental validation, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为进一步研究HMPV 疫苗的开发奠定了基础,这可能有助于改善监测、诊断以及HMPV相关呼吸道感染的预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于计算方法,未包括实验验证,因此证据强度受到一定限制。

Molecular docking and MD simulations showed that there is a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of − 14.6 and immune activation. Moreover, the disulfide engineering enhanced construct stability. Cloning and codon optimization was used to verify efficient expression in the target host. Taken together, these findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen of HMPV.

title: Retrospective analysis of multiplex panel tests in the diagnosis of respiratory tract infections
abstract: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) remain a major global health concern, particularly in children. The overlapping clinical manifestations of RTIs highlight the need for rapid and accurate diagnostic methods such as multiplex PCR (mPCR). This retrospective single-center study investigated the epidemiology of respiratory pathogens detected by mPCR, focusing on their distribution, age-related patterns, seasonal variation, and coinfections. Nasopharyngeal swab samples from 328 patients with suspected acute RTIs, collected between January 2022 and December 2023, were analyzed using the BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, pathogen distribution, seasonal trends, and coinfections were evaluated. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 270 of 328 specimens, yielding an overall positivity rate of 82.3%. Viral pathogens predominated; human rhinovirus/enterovirus HRV/HEV (28%), adenovirus (21.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (14.2%), and influenza viruses (11.3%) were the most frequently identified agents. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) were detected in 6.8% and 5.8% of cases, respectively. The vast majority of specimens (91.5%) were from pediatric patients (0–18 years). Coinfections were identified in 31.8% of positive cases, most commonly involving adenovirus and HRV/HEV. Seasonal analysis demonstrated a marked increase in positivity during winter and spring months, accounting for 74% of all positive cases. Bacterial pathogens were rarely detected. mPCR demonstrated high diagnostic value, with pathogens detected in 82.3% of samples, predominantly viral agents. These findings support the role of mPCR in improving diagnostic accuracy and providing valuable regional epidemiological data. Rapid identification of viral pathogens may also support antimicrobial stewardship by facilitating more informed clinical decision-making; however, antibiotic utilization was not evaluated in the present study.
journal: Reviews and Research in Medical Microbiology

abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染(RTIs)仍然是全球主要的健康问题,尤其是在儿童中。RTIs的重叠临床表现凸显了需要快速准确的诊断方法,如多重PCR(mPCR)。本回顾性单中心研究调查了mPCR检测到的流行病学呼吸道病原体,重点关注其分布、年龄相关模式、季节性变化和混合感染情况。使用BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1分析了2022年1月至2023年12月期间收集的328例疑似急性RTI患者的鼻咽拭子样本。评估了人口统计学特征、临床发现、病原体分布、季节趋势和混合感染情况。在328份样本中,至少检测到一种呼吸道病原体的有270份,总体阳性率为82.3%。病毒病原体占主导地位;人类鼻病毒/肠病毒HRV/HEV(28%)、腺病毒(21.8%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)(14.2%)和流感病毒(11.3%)是最常检测到的病原体。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)和人类副流感病毒(HMPV)分别在6.8%和5.8%的病例中被检测到。绝大多数样本(91.5%)来自儿科患者(0-18岁)。在阳性病例中,有31.8%出现了混合感染,最常见的混合感染涉及腺病毒和HRV/HEV。季节性分析显示,在冬季和春季的阳性率显著增加,占所有阳性病例的74%。细菌病原体很少被检测到。mPCR表现出高诊断价值,在82.3%的样本中检测到了病原体,主要为病毒病原体。这些发现支持mPCR在提高诊断准确性并提供有价值的区域流行病学数据中的作用。快速识别病毒病原体可能也有助于抗菌药物的合理使用,通过促进更明智的临床决策;然而,本研究未评估抗生素的使用情况。

title: RSV Vaccination in Systemic Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination is available for older adults. Patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), including those receiving immunosuppressive therapies, were excluded from trials. Evidence to guide vaccination decisions is limited. We conducted a systematic review evaluating RSV epidemiology, vaccine effectiveness, immunogenicity, and safety in adults with SARDs. Databases were searched from inception to 28th January 2026. Observational studies, clinical trials, and pharmacovigilance reports were included. Evidence specific to disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) was examined where available. Of the 249 unique records returned, 43 met the inclusion criteria. Six studies were identified in the supplementary search, yielding 49 studies in total. Only one study reported RSV outcomes in SARD patients. No study evaluated vaccine effectiveness stratified by DMARD-class. Observational data suggest autoimmune and immunocompromising conditions are associated with increased RSV-associated hospitalisation, although attribution is uncertain due to bias and data limitations. RSV vaccines demonstrated first-season effectiveness of 60–73% in immunocompromised adults, with evidence of attenuated and more rapidly waning protection compared with immunocompetent populations. Immunogenicity studies from RSV and other vaccine platforms indicate reduced seroconversion in immunosuppressed patients. No consistent autoimmune safety signals were identified, though data in SARD populations remain limited. RSV poses a relevant, though incompletely quantified, risk for SARD patients. Vaccination appears effective and safe in immunocompromised populations, but protection may wane more rapidly. The absence of DMARD-specific data represents an evidence gap. Until further evidence emerges, vaccination should be considered for eligible patients using a personalised framework.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疫苗接种在老年人群中可用。本综述聚焦于系统性自身免疫风湿性疾病(SARDs)患者,包括接受免疫抑制治疗的患者,这些患者被排除在试验之外的疫苗接种情况。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 进行了一项系统综述,评估RSV 流行病学、疫苗在SARDs成人患者中的有效性、免疫原性和安全性。检索数据库的时间范围是从起始日期到2026年1月28日,分析中纳入了49项研究,包括观察性研究、临床试验和药物不良反应报告。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 没有研究评估疫苗在不同DMARD类别中的有效性。缺乏DMARD特异性数据代表了证据缺口。注意到研究设计的异质性以及在SARD患者中关于安全性和有效性的数据有限。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 疫苗接种在免疫抑制人群中似乎有效且安全,但保护效果可能消退更快。在进一步证据出现之前,应考虑对符合条件的患者采用个性化框架使用疫苗接种。

title: Maternal RSV vaccination: clinical efficacy, safety, and global policy considerations: a systematic review.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is among the leading causes of lower respiratory tract illness in newborns worldwide. This study reviews evidence on the efficacy and safety of maternal RSV vaccination. Methods PROSPERO registered this PRISMA-compliant systematic review (CRD42024566335). Keywords associated with RSV, respiratory infections, newborns, and immunisation were used in a search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL (inception to mid-2026). Because of the heterogeneity of the studies, a descriptive synthesis of the safety and efficacy data was performed instead of a formal meta-analysis. Results Sixteen publications – four real-world studies and twelve generated from nine separate parent trials/datasets (including three subgroup or subset analyses and post-hoc studies from two RCTs) – met the inclusion criteria. Depending on the dose, formulation, and length of follow-up, maternal immunisation was linked to a lower incidence of severe RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections in newborns, with efficacy/effectiveness varying from roughly 39% to 100%. Trial-based efficacy results were generally in line with real-world effectiveness data from national and multicenter initiatives in the US, UK, and Argentina. Preterm birth outcomes differed depending on the formulation: a bivalent RSVpreF vaccine (Pfizer MATISSE trial; [Li, Y., Wang, X., Blau, D. Global, regional, and national disease burden estimates of acute lower respiratory infections due to respiratory syncytial virus in children younger than 5 years in 2019: A systematic analysis. The Lancet, 399(10340), 2047–2064; Otsuki, T., Akada, S., Anami, A., Kosaka, K., Munjal, I., Baber, J., Shoji, Y., Aizawa, M., Swanson, K. Efficacy and safety of bivalent RSVpreF maternal vaccination to prevent RSV illness in Japanese infants: Subset analysis from the pivotal randomized phase 3 MATISSE trial. Vaccine, 42(22), 126041]) did not exhibit this association in post-hoc analyses, while an unadjuvanted RSVpreF vaccine (GSK; [Dieussaert, I., Hyung Kim, J., Luik, S., Seidl, C., Pu, W., Stegmann, J.-U., Swamy, G. K., Webster, P., & Dormitzer, P. RSV prefusion F protein–based maternal vaccine – preterm birth and other outcomes. New England Journal of Medicine, 390(11), 1009–1021]) showed a significant increase in preterm birth (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.08–1.74). Although post-vaccination responses were frequent, they were usually mild to moderate. Conclusion There was no discernible rise in major adverse outcomes for mothers or newborns. Real-world data from a variety of situations now supports the conclusion that maternal RSV vaccination consistently decreased newborn RSV hospitalisation and severe disease. However, ongoing post-marketing surveillance and formulation-specific safety reporting are necessary due to variations in preterm birth risk that rely on timing and formulation.
journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice

This study reviews evidence on the efficacy and safety of maternal RSV vaccination. Methods PROSPERO registered this PRISMA-compliant systematic review (CRD42024566335). Keywords associated with RSV, respiratory infections, newborns, and immunisation were used in a search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL (inception to mid-2026). Because of the heterogeneity of the studies, a descriptive synthesis of the safety and efficacy data was performed instead of a formal meta-analysis. Results Sixteen publications – four real-world studies and twelve generated from nine separate parent trials/datasets (including three subgroup or subset analyses and post-hoc studies from two RCTs) – met the inclusion criteria. Depending on the dose, formulation, and length of follow-up, maternal immunisation was linked to a lower incidence of severe RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections in newborns, with efficacy/effectiveness varying from roughly 39% to 100%. Trial-based efficacy results were generally in line with real-world effectiveness data from national and multicenter initiatives in the US, UK, and Argentina. Preterm birth outcomes differed depending on the formulation: a bivalent RSVpreF vaccine (Pfizer MATISSE trial; [Li, Y., Wang, X., Blau, D. Global, regional, and national disease burden estimates of acute lower respiratory infections due to respiratory syncytial virus in children younger than 5 years in 2019: A systematic analysis. The Lancet, 399(10340), 2047–2064; Otsuki, T., Akada, S., Anami, A., Kosaka, K., Munjal, I., Baber, J., Shoji, Y., Aizawa, M., Swanson, K. Efficacy and safety of bivalent RSVpreF maternal vaccination to prevent RSV illness in Japanese infants: Subset analysis from the pivotal randomized phase 3 MATISSE trial. Vaccine, 42(22), 126041]) did not exhibit this association in post-hoc analyses, while an unadjuvanted RSVpreF vaccine (GSK; [Dieussaert, I., Hyung Kim, J., Luik, S., Seidl, C., Pu, W., Stegmann, J.-U., Swamy, G. K., Webster, P., & Dormitzer, P. RSV prefusion F protein–based maternal vaccine – preterm birth and other outcomes. New England Journal of Medicine, 390(11), 1009–1021]) showed a significant increase in preterm birth (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.08–1.74). Although post-vaccination responses were frequent, they were usually mild to moderate. Conclusion There was no discernible rise in major adverse outcomes for mothers or newborns. Real-world data from a variety of situations now supports the conclusion that maternal RSV vaccination consistently decreased newborn RSV hospitalisation and severe disease. However, ongoing post-marketing surveillance and formulation-specific safety reporting are necessary due to variations in preterm birth risk that rely on timing and formulation.

title: SARS-CoV-2 and RSV external quality assessment on molecular detection and variant typing in European expert laboratories in 2025.
abstract: ABSTRACT We herein report on the fourth SARS-CoV-2 wet-lab external quality assessment (EQA) and the second organized by the AURORAE consortium to assess the diagnostic capabilities of European expert public health laboratories. Diagnostic capabilities were investigated regarding SARS-CoV-2 and, for the first time, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) groups A and B. A 10-sample panel containing various SARS-CoV-2 variants, RSV lineages, a common cold coronavirus, and a negative control was produced and validated. Participants were invited by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) and asked to submit results and assay details via electronic forms. Thirty-seven laboratories from 32 European countries participated. All panel samples were identified correctly via molecular detection by 23 participating laboratories (23/37; 62%). Commercial assays were used most often (23/37; 62%), in comparison to in-house assays (14/37; 38%), or a combination of both (8/37; 22%). RSV groups were correctly determined by 20 laboratories (20/37; 54%). The optional task of SARS-CoV-2 variant typing was performed by 20 laboratories using next-generation sequencing. Thirteen laboratories successfully generated SARS-CoV-2 sequences. Six laboratories performed optional RSV sequencing, with only two obtaining sequences. The current and previous EQAs show that molecular detection of SARS-CoV-2 within Europe has improved over time and is now at a consistently high level. Molecular detection of RSV samples with low viral load was challenging, as was lineage identification for low-concentration specimens. Routine monitoring of diagnostic and surveillance assays via EQAs remains key to maintaining rapid and long-lasting public health laboratory response systems. IMPORTANCE External quality assessments (EQAs) are essential for ensuring reliable and consistent diagnostic testing. They provide an objective way to evaluate laboratory performance, identify weaknesses, and drive improvements, as well as ensuring compliance with accreditation standards. Furthermore, participating in EQAs strengthens the contributions to public health disease surveillance and threat detection on national and transborder scales. During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, EQAs were vital for maintaining accuracy in the setting of increasing testing demands and emerging variants. Broadening of diagnostic testing to a wider panel of viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), requires continuous performance monitoring to ensure accuracy and reliability. Ongoing development of vaccines and therapeutics, which may drive the emergence of new mutations, further underscores the need for regular evaluation of test effectiveness. By standardizing methods and reducing errors, EQAs ensure trustworthy and comparable results across laboratories. Regular participation in EQAs strengthens molecular diagnostics and variant surveillance.

title: Epidemiology of human RSV in Taiwan, 2018-2024.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and older adults worldwide. This retrospective study investigated the epidemiology and molecular characteristics of RSV in Taiwan from 2018 to 2024 using data from the National Community Virus Surveillance System, which encompassed the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period. Among 74,773 samples collected from patients with suspected respiratory viral infections, 1,224 samples tested positive for RSV, yielding an overall detection rate of 1.6%. RSV circulation was markedly disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic, with no cases being detected during periods of stringent public health interventions and delayed outbreaks observed in late 2020 and 2023. Following the relaxation of nonpharmaceutical interventions, RSV seasonality shifted, with altered epidemic timing and changes in age distribution being observed. Most infections occurred in children younger than 5 years of age (92.6%), and RSV positivity varied significantly across age groups but not between sexes. Among the 1,224 isolates, 463 were randomly selected for glycoprotein (G) gene sequencing. The results revealed that RSV-A accounted for the majority (81.6%) of the tested isolates and were clustered within the A.D lineage, with A.D.3 being the dominant clade. The remaining strains were determined to be RSV-B, which were classified within the B.D lineage, with B.D.E.1 being observed as the dominant clade. The emergence of multiple RSV subclades during the study period indicates ongoing viral evolution in Taiwan. These findings demonstrate substantial shifts in RSV epidemiology following the COVID-19 pandemic and highlight viral evolution and clade replacement. Continued molecular surveillance is essential to monitor epidemiological trends and inform vaccination and prevention strategies.

title: Efficacy and safety of maternal RSV vaccination against infant lower respiratory tract infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of infant lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) and hospitalisation worldwide. Maternal RSV prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccination protects infants through transplacental antibody transfer. We aimed to synthesise the efficacy, real-world effectiveness, and safety of maternal RSV vaccination for preventing infant LRTI, integrating randomised and observational evidence. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL (to June 2026) for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies of maternal RSV vaccination reporting infant LRTI, hospitalisation, or maternal–infant safety. A single reviewer, with large language model-assisted verification, screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2; Newcastle–Ottawa Scale). Randomised and observational evidence were pooled separately using random-effects models; overlapping populations were resolved based on study periods and named participating sites. Certainty was rated with GRADE (PROSPERO CRD420261400053). Results Twenty-four studies (9 RCTs enrolling approximately 18,600 pregnant women, 15 observational) were included; all 15 observational studies evaluated the licensed Pfizer vaccine (Abrysvo). Pooled vaccine effectiveness against infant RSV-associated hospitalisation was 79.7% (95% CI 73.9–84.2) within 3 months and 68.1% (57.1–76.3) through 6 months. Randomised efficacy against severe RSV-LRTI was 70% for the licensed Pfizer vaccine, closely concordant with the real-world effectiveness; efficacy against medically attended RSV-LRTI was 51.5% (36.3–63.1). Preterm birth was modestly increased in the randomised trials (Mantel–Haenszel RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.03–1.32), but the signal was not robust: it became non-significant after excluding the GSK trial (GRACE; 1.10, 0.95–1.27), and for the licensed Pfizer vaccine, the increase was small and not robustly significant (pivotal MATISSE trial 1.20, 0.98–1.46; three-trial Pfizer pool 1.21, 1.00–1.46), while observational data showed a biologically implausible protective association (0.90, 0.82–0.99), consistent with healthy vaccinee confounding. No other maternal or neonatal safety signal was identified. Certainty of evidence was moderate for effectiveness and efficacy. Conclusion Maternal RSVpreF vaccination confers substantial, generalisable protection against infant RSV disease, with randomised and real-world evidence in close agreement. For the licensed Pfizer vaccine administered within its approved 32–36-week window, no robustly significant increase in preterm birth is established, supporting its continued programmatic use alongside ongoing post-marketing surveillance. Systematic review registration Unique Identifier: CRD420261400053 https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261400053

title: Multicenter evaluation of Coyote FlashDetect LyocartE multiplex assays for six respiratory pathogens: a comparative analysis with Sansure and Cepheid assays.
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory diseases caused by common respiratory pathogens, such as influenza A/B (Flu A/B), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), adenovirus (ADV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), share many of the same symptoms and may progress to severe complications in some cases. Multiplex molecular point-of-care testing (mPOCT) enables automated and rapid differential diagnosis for timely intervention. This study independently evaluated the clinical performance of Coyote FlashDetect LyocartE SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB and FlashDetect LyocartE RSV/MP/ADV multiplex mPOCT assays using the Sansure as the primary comparator, followed by a subset-based, target-specific paired comparison with Cepheid mPOCT assay for selected respiratory pathogens (FluA, FluB, and RSV). Specifically, 642 and 427 throat swab specimens were used to evaluate the Coyote SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB and Coyote RSV/MP/ADV multiplex mPOCT assays against Sansure assays, respectively. Coyote assays demonstrated high concordance with Sansure assays, with overall percent agreement (OPA) values ranging from 93.8% to 100.0% for six pathogens covered by two Coyote assays. Most discrepancies with Sansure assays occurred in samples with cycle threshold (Ct) values ≥35, especially among FluA samples. Moreover, 414, 414, and 215 specimens were allocated for FluA, FluB, and RSV, respectively, to conduct target-specific paired comparison between Coyote and Cepheid. Each Coyote assay also demonstrated high concordance with the Cepheid assays, with PPA values of 96.0%, 100.0%, and 98.3% for FluA, FluB, and RSV, respectively. These results support the use of Coyote mPOCT assays in specific settings. Coyote assays demonstrated a high degree of concordance for shared targets with comparator methods, supporting their use as a rapid and user-friendly diagnostic approach for multiplex respiratory pathogen detection. IMPORTANCE This study highlights the value of multiplex molecular point-of-care tests. The POCT assays demonstrate high concordance with the laboratory-based lab tests in this retrospective specimen cohort, offering a viable, rapid, and user-friendly alternative for multiplex respiratory pathogen detection and hold the promise to be used in primary healthcare settings and public health surveillance.

This study independently evaluated the clinical performance of Coyote FlashDetect LyocartE SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB and FlashDetect LyocartE RSV/MP/ADV multiplex mPOCT assays using the Sansure as the primary comparator, followed by a subset-based, target-specific paired comparison with Cepheid mPOCT assay for selected respiratory pathogens (FluA, FluB, and RSV). Specifically, 642 and 427 throat swab specimens were used to evaluate the Coyote SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB and Coyote RSV/MP/ADV multiplex mPOCT assays against Sansure assays, respectively. Coyote assays demonstrated high concordance with Sansure assays, with overall percent agreement (OPA) values ranging from 93.8% to 100.0% for six pathogens covered by two Coyote assays. Most discrepancies with Sansure assays occurred in samples with cycle threshold (Ct) values ≥35, especially among FluA samples. Moreover, 414, 414, and 215 specimens were allocated for FluA, FluB, and RSV, respectively, to conduct target-specific paired comparison between Coyote and Cepheid. Each Coyote assay also demonstrated high concordance with the Cepheid assays, with PPA values of 96.0%, 100.0%, and 98.3% for FluA, FluB, and RSV, respectively. These results support the use of Coyote mPOCT assays in specific settings. title: From Infant Protection to Healthy Respiratory Aging: Potential Long-Term Benefits of RSV Prevention in Latin America and the Caribbean
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of infant lower respiratory tract infection, hospitalization, and death in Latin America and the Caribbean, where unequal access to diagnosis, medical care, oxygen, referral, and intensive care worsens outcomes. New passive immunization tools, maternal RSV prefusion F vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies, can protect infants before peak vulnerability. Still, their population impact depends on timing, coverage, equity, financing, surveillance, and program design. Emerging regional experience with hybrid strategies may help close protection gaps among infants missed or insufficiently protected by maternal immunization. Severe early-life RSV disease is consistently associated with recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, wheezing, asthma, impaired lung-function trajectories, and increased health-care use. However, causality and long-term effects of current preventive products remain uncertain. A regional agenda linking maternal-infant cohorts, surveillance, equity analyses, and life-course economic evaluation is needed to define the full public health value of RSV prevention.

title: Epidemiological analysis of respiratory and enteric outbreaks in long-term care homes in Ontario, Canada from 2020 to 2025. A retrospective longitudinal cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Outbreaks of respiratory and enteric infections constitute a major threat to residents in long-term care (LTC) homes. The aim of the study was to analyze the epidemiological characteristics of respiratory and enteric outbreaks during and after the COVID-19 pandemic in order to provide a scientific basis for infection prevention and control strategies. METHODS: This retrospective, longitudinal cross-sectional study examined respiratory and enteric outbreaks across 25 LTC homes in Ontario, Canada from 2020 to 2025. The difference in pathogen distribution by month, season and year was examined. Outbreaks were categorized by phase: pandemic (2020-2022) and post-pandemic (2023-2025) and categorical distributions were analyzed using Chi-Square tests. RESULTS: The pandemic phase was dominated by SARS-CoV-2 with widespread suppression of other viruses, whereas the post-pandemic era saw a multi-pathogen resurgence. Post-pandemic, Influenza and RSV outbreaks peaked from October-March while Rhinovirus showed multiple seasonal peaks. The mean duration of outbreak ranged from 9.81 - 18.72 days and the mean attack rate ranged from 6.76 - 22.05%. CONCLUSIONS: The post-COVID-19 pandemic in LTC homes in Ontario is defined by a complex multi-pathogen burden. SARS-CoV-2 was not suppressed post-pandemic but remained as a major cause of outbreak in this setting with year-round circulation and Winter peaks. Influenza and RSV maintained Winter seasonality. Protecting residents in LTC homes requires a sustainable multi-pathogen surveillance strategy.

Methods This retrospective, longitudinal cross-sectional study examined respiratory and enteric outbreaks across 25 LTC homes in Ontario, Canada from 2020 to 2025. The difference in pathogen distribution by month, season and year was examined. Outbreaks were categorized by phase: pandemic (2020-2022) and post-pandemic (2023-2025) and categorical distributions were analyzed using Chi-Square tests. Results The pandemic phase was dominated by SARS-CoV-2 with widespread suppression of other viruses, whereas the post-pandemic era saw a multi-pathogen resurgence. Post-pandemic, Influenza and RSV outbreaks peaked from October-March while Rhinovirus showed multiple seasonal peaks. The mean duration of outbreak ranged from 9.81 - 18.72 days and the mean attack rate ranged from 6.76 - 22.05%. Conclusions The post-COVID-19 pandemic in LTC homes in Ontario is defined by a complex multi-pathogen burden. SARS-CoV-2 was not suppressed post-pandemic but remained as a major cause of outbreak in this setting with year-round circulation and Winter peaks. Influenza and RSV maintained Winter seasonality. Protecting residents in LTC homes requires a sustainable multi-pathogen surveillance strategy.
